newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela Cretacico oil sale cancelled as no bids.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela Cretacico oil sale cancelled as no bids.

text.p: Venezuelan state owned oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) canceled the scheduled Wednesday auction of the Cretacico Sur oil field in western Venezuela after no bids were received, a PDVSA spokesman said.
Operating rights were to be sold as part of Venezuela's on- going third oil contracts auction round. The round has so far attracted higher-than-expected bids.
However, PDVSA's exploration and production coordinator Juan Szabo told reporters Venezuela "would probably offer the field up again in the near future." He did not give a time frame.
Szabo added investors were probably deterred by the field's size, geological complexity, high level of required investment and lack of time to adequately study the block.
"We'll have to sit down and see if time was a problem ... if the formula has to modified," he said.
The 784 square km field, discovered in Lake Maracaibo in 1967, currently produces 500 barrels per day from one active well and 30-50 million barrels of proven reserves.
As a condition of the contract, the bidder would have had to invest at least $50 million within four years.
The auction was the first to draw no bids after earlier sales attracted offers totaling more than $1.2 billion.
A total of 131 companies are competing for 20 contracts to be sold this week with the winners determined purely by the size of their bids.
